Hi Ben,

Attached is a short forecast (NovaHealth_Demand_Forecast_Q2-Q4.xlsx). Can you share viable paths and any timelines you need from our side to get capacity online?

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai

Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity bump & co-term question

Hi Samantha — thanks for the forecast and the heads-up. Short answer: we can support your ramp with three operationally distinct paths depending on how risk vs. cost you want the outcome to be. I’ve summarized options and next steps below; I’ve also attached a one-pager (redwood_uplift_options.pdf) that frames tradeoffs.

Options (high level)
1) Immediate top-up (fastest):
  - Add dedicated capacity now at standard uplift pricing (no contract term change).
  - Time to serve: ~48–72 hrs after PO.
  - Cost: list rate for additional units; no discount.
  - Pros: zero coordination on contract; immediate throughput.
  - Cons: higher unit cost; renews on original contract cadence.

2) Staged voucher + scheduled co-term (balanced):
  - Issue a 6-month voucher for excess usage (applies as credit) combined with a scoped amendment to annualize the added capacity and co-term to Feb 1.
  - Discount: 6% on the annualized units if NovaHealth signs the amendment within 60 days.
  - Time to serve: voucher applied within 24 hours, capacity provisioned within 5 business days.
  - Pros: immediate relief, predictable unit economics if you commit.

3) Annualize now with blended uplift (commit-forward):
  - Convert the projected uplift into committed units for the remainder of the contract year and move to a blended rate (one-time mid-contract addendum).
  - Discount: up to 12% depending on final volume band and payment timing.
  - Time to serve: provisioning in 5–7 business days; legal and procurement lead time for amendment.

Ask from NovaHealth to proceed
  - Preferred path (1/2/3)
  - Signed PO or internal approval timeline
  - Confirmation of co-term target (I have Feb 1 marked; confirm if you want a different date)

I’ve cc’d Irene (sales ops) to scope billing flow and Marissa for approvals on any above-list concessions. If helpful I can lay these into a short mutual-action plan and a draft DocuSign amendment.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-1212

Marissa — forwarding the thread and the forecast. NovaHealth is leaning toward option 2 (staged voucher + scheduled co-term) but asked whether we can increase the near-term voucher value and give a ‘‘sign-by’’ discount. They sign fast if we can move to a 10% pledge discount; procurement pushed for more.

My recommendation: approve up to 8% for a signed amendment within 45 days (require PO for voucher). If we want to protect margin, we hold 12% for a firm higher-volume commit (option 3).

Notes for ops: Irene, can you outline what the billing flow looks like if we issue a voucher that auto-applies to overage and how we reconcile when the amendment is signed? I’d like a one-sentence external line item for DocuSign: "Issuance of a six-month service voucher for excess usage, credit applied to invoice until consumed; remainder converts to committed units upon amendment execution."

Thanks — Ben
